# Self-Improving AI

A skill lifecycle for OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex. It turns useful lessons
from completed work into reusable Agent Skills.

It does not retrain the model. It writes and maintains instructions that the
model can use on later tasks.

## Memory and skills

The loop has two durable outputs:

- Memory stores facts, decisions, preferences, corrections, and ongoing context.
- Skills store reusable procedures, decision rules, tool usage, and verification.

It pairs naturally with [GBrain](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain): GBrain
provides the memory layer, while this starting skill grows and refines the
procedural skill layer. GBrain is optional; agents without it can use their
existing memory mechanism.

## Install

Each adapter uses the model and credentials already configured in its client.
There is no second provider account or API key to set up.

### OpenCode

Install the skill globally for OpenCode:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/hueyexe/self-improving-ai \
  --skill self-improving --agent opencode --global --yes
```

Append this entry to the existing `plugin` array in
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. Keep your other plugin entries:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["self-improving-opencode@latest"]
}
```

Use the tuple form only when overriding defaults:

```json
[
  "self-improving-opencode@latest",
  {
    "minToolCalls": 10,
    "correctedMinToolCalls": 5,
    "readOnlyMinToolCalls": 20,
    "staleAfterDays": 30,
    "archiveAfterDays": 90,
    "curatorIntervalDays": 7,
    "debug": false
  }
]
```

Fully quit and restart OpenCode after changing the config. OpenCode installs the
package from npm when it starts.

### Claude Code

Install the skill globally for Claude Code:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/hueyexe/self-improving-ai \
  --skill self-improving --agent claude-code --global --yes
```

Then add the plugin marketplace and install the completion adapter inside
Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add hueyexe/self-improving-ai
/plugin install self-improving@self-improving-ai
```

Start a new session after installation. After the transcript reaches 12,000
bytes, the hook launches a detached `claude -p` review using the user's existing
Claude Code model and credentials. If detached execution is unavailable, it
falls back to the guarded in-session completion check.

### Codex

Install the skill globally for Codex:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/hueyexe/self-improving-ai \
  --skill self-improving --agent codex --global --yes
```

Then add the plugin marketplace and install the completion adapter:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add hueyexe/self-improving-ai
codex plugin add self-improving@self-improving-ai
```

Open `/hooks` in Codex and trust the new hook, then start a new thread. The
adapter launches a detached `codex exec` review after the transcript reaches
12,000 bytes, using the user's existing Codex model, provider, and credentials.
If detached execution is unavailable, it falls back to the guarded in-session
completion check.

### Other agents

Other clients can use the skill without an automatic completion adapter. Install
it for every client supported by the Skills CLI:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/hueyexe/self-improving-ai --all --global
```

**OpenCode note:** the global agent-compatible location opencode v2 reads is
`~/.agents/skills/` (one of six search paths — https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/).
If the Skills CLI writes elsewhere for your setup, copy
`skills/self-improving/` to `~/.agents/skills/self-improving/` manually.
OpenCode requires a restart to see skills added while it is running
(Skill.state caches per process).

Eve and PromptScript currently report failures because they do not support
global skill installation. Other supported clients still install successfully.

## OpenCode background flow

The plugin records tool activity during a session. This is a small local JSON
update; it does not call a model after every tool use.

When the session becomes idle, the plugin checks the work since the previous
review. A review is queued after:

- 10 tool calls when files changed;
- 5 tool calls when failures were encountered;
- 20 tool calls for read-only work.

**Idle detection (v0.3.0):** interactive sessions emit `session.idle`, but
headless `opencode run` finishes with `session.execution.{succeeded,failed,interrupted}` instead — verified empirically on v2.0.5, a full headless run emits no `session.idle` at all. The plugin now treats both shapes (plus the `session.status`+`idle` variant) as review triggers, so reviews queue in either mode.

The queued job opens an isolated OpenCode child session with the same provider
and model as the parent session. The child has no tools. It reads the relevant
conversation and returns one structured decision: create a skill, patch a
managed skill, or do nothing.

**The model never applies its own proposals (v0.3.0).** Plugin code checks the
response, rejects unsafe paths and changes to unmanaged skills, and writes it
as a **pending proposal** to `~/.local/share/self-improving-ai/proposals/`.
Nothing is applied to your skills directories until a human runs:

```
self-improving-ai proposals            # list pending proposals with diffs
self-improving-ai proposals apply <id>
self-improving-ai proposals reject <id>
```

This is the safe-inheritance gate from the RSI literature (unattended
self-modification regresses in a nontrivial share of trials — *The Last AI
Built by Humans*, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11873 §6; *Dream-RSI*,
https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14858) and mirrors the Warp production skill loop:
inner skill does work, outer reviewer proposes, human merges. A Hermes-side
companion cron (`~/.hermes/scripts/skill_improver_scan.py`) also surfaces
pending proposals weekly. The child session is deleted when the review ends.

Interrupted jobs are retried up to three times after a restart.

This work happens after idle and does not block the conversation. It does use a
model call when a review threshold is reached. Ordinary chat and short sessions
do not trigger one.

## Files and ownership

State is stored under `~/.local/share/self-improving-ai/` by default. Skill
files remain under `~/.agents/skills/`, where OpenCode and other clients can find
them. Generated skills are marked in `SKILL.md`:

```yaml
metadata:
  managed-by: self-improving-ai
  provenance: self-improving
  maturity: candidate
```

The state directory contains the review queue, registry, audit log, session
counters, backups, and archived skills. Only skills created by this plugin or
explicitly adopted by the user are managed. Other installed and hand-written
skills are left alone. Pinned skills are also left alone.

Managed skills become stale after 30 days without use and are moved to the
recoverable archive after 90 days. Curation runs at most once a week. It never
deletes, commits, pushes, or publishes anything.

## Manage the lifecycle

Inspect and manage the lifecycle with the package CLI:

```bash
npx self-improving-opencode status
npx self-improving-opencode dry-run
npx self-improving-opencode consolidation-report
npx self-improving-opencode pin api-error-triage
npx self-improving-opencode unpin api-error-triage
npx self-improving-opencode adopt existing-skill ~/.agents/skills/existing-skill
npx self-improving-opencode archive api-error-triage
npx self-improving-opencode restore api-error-triage
```

`consolidation-report` performs a conservative, read-only overlap scan of
managed skills. It reports possible duplicates but does not merge them.

## Claude Code and Codex

Claude Code and Codex review at most once per session. Both default to a
12,000-byte transcript threshold. Their detached workers use the model and
credentials configured in the client. Claude Code disables reviewer tools;
Codex runs the reviewer in its read-only sandbox.

### Optional [GBrain](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain) context

For Claude Code or Codex, enable GBrain context for their completion review by
setting this environment variable before launching the client:

```bash
export SELF_IMPROVING_GBRAIN=1
```

Reviewers currently handle procedural skills only; they do not write factual
memory. This flag does not install or configure GBrain. Follow the
[GBrain repository](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain) for setup. The flag only
tells the review to use GBrain, when available, for durable non-procedural
memory while keeping procedures in Agent Skills.

Claude Code and Codex threshold overrides:

```bash
export SELF_IMPROVING_MIN_TRANSCRIPT_BYTES=12000 # Claude Code and Codex
```

Set the transcript threshold to `0` to review every Claude Code or Codex
session. Lower thresholds increase cost and low-value skill churn.

Set OpenCode's `debug` option to `true`, or set `SELF_IMPROVING_DEBUG=1`, to
record activity decisions and review outcomes in the OpenCode log.
Debug logging does not add messages to the session.

## Manage the skill

List the installed skill and its source:

```bash
npx skills list --global
```

Update it from GitHub:

```bash
npx skills update self-improving --global --yes
```

Remove it:

```bash
npx skills remove self-improving --global --yes
```

## Release the OpenCode package

Maintainers publish releases explicitly. Update `version` in `package.json`,
then run:

```bash
bun run check
bun test
bun run build
bun publish --access public
git tag -a "v$(bun -p 'require("./package.json").version')" -m "Release"
git push origin main --follow-tags
gh release create "v$(bun -p 'require("./package.json").version')" \
  --generate-notes --verify-tag
```

## Skill conventions

- `skills/self-improving` is the only starting skill.
- Skills created by the loop use clear capability-based names.
- Generated skills carry controlled provenance and maturity metadata so they
  remain easy to identify and export. Skills may also define their own category
  and scope metadata.
- New workflows start as `candidate`, become `validated` after focused testing
  or successful reuse, and become `proven` after repeated use.
- Repository-specific procedures remain with their repository rather than being
  generalized into this collection.

Each directory under `skills/` follows the [Agent Skills
specification](https://agentskills.io/specification).
